title: 23. Enterprise Integrations
description: Turing S4 core: webhooks, SSO (SAML/OIDC/SCIM), OAuth bridging, VPC-private deployment, HIPAA/SOC2 constraints, legacy ERP adapters. What FDEs actually build for enterprise customers.

23.2 SSO: SAML, OIDC, SCIM: SCIM v2 for lifecycle (create / update / deactivate)
23.4 VPC / Private Deploy: No third-party dependencies from data plane
23.6 Legacy System Adapters: Read replica > CDC > file drops > screen-scrape (in that order)
Contracts on the boundary, not through it

questions.prompt: Design an OUTBOUND webhook system: you deliver events to 10k customer endpoints, some flaky. At-least-once + no lost events.

rubric.criterion: Outbox pattern — write event to DB in same txn as source op
Separate worker fleet drains outbox to HTTP delivery
Exp backoff (1s, 4s, 15s, 1m, 5m, 30m, cap 24h) + jitter
HMAC signature (payload + timestamp) so customer can verify
Idempotency key so retries safe on receiver side
DLQ + replay UI after N retries
Per-endpoint circuit breaker to avoid wasting workers on down endpoints

questions.modelAnswer: Producers write event + delivery row to outbox table in same txn. Worker fleet polls outbox, POSTs with `X-Signature: hmac-sha256(secret, ts + body)`, `X-Timestamp`, `X-Idempotency-Key`. Exp backoff with jitter after each failure; move to DLQ after 8 attempts + alert. Per-endpoint circuit breaker: if fail rate > 50% over 5 min, open circuit for 10 min. Replay UI reads DLQ, allows manual retry or bulk resend on customer request.

questions.prompt: Design an INBOUND webhook ingestion engine: 100k events/sec, per-tenant rate limits, retry backoffs, tenant isolation.

rubric.criterion: Edge: ALB + TLS + HMAC verify + fast 202 response
Thin ingest handler → Kafka partitioned by tenant_id
Per-tenant rate limit at edge (Redis token bucket)
Consumer fleet auto-scales on partition lag
Idempotency check (dedup on event_id in Redis SETNX with TTL)
Per-tenant DLQ + replay UI
Capacity math: 100k × 1KB = 100MB/s → ~8.6TB/day

questions.modelAnswer: See stage 09 sd-013 for the full canonical answer. Edge → ALB → nginx (TLS, HMAC verify, per-tenant Redis token bucket) → 3-tier ingest fleet. Ingest: verify HMAC, check idempotency (SETNX), write to Kafka partitioned by tenant_id (256 partitions), return 202. Consumers per tenant scale on lag. DLQ Kafka topic per tenant. Ops UI to replay. Sizing: 6 brokers RF=3, 7-day retention ≈ 25TB. Alert on ingest 5xx, HMAC failures, per-tenant lag, DLQ depth.

questions.prompt: Customer's webhook receiver is down 30% of the time. Don't overwhelm them + don't lose events. Design.

rubric.criterion: Circuit breaker per endpoint
Backoff scales with sustained failure rate, not just per-request
Adaptive concurrency: reduce workers hitting that endpoint
Health signal loop: probe request on schedule when circuit open
Communicate to customer proactively

questions.modelAnswer: Circuit breaker per endpoint: closed (normal) → open (skip requests) after 20 failures in 5 min → half-open (probe request every 60s) → closed on 3 consecutive successes. Adaptive concurrency limits workers hitting flaky endpoint to 1 while circuit is degraded. Emit customer-facing metric so their ops team sees delivery lag rising. Proactive outreach: 'we noticed your endpoint has 30% error rate — anything we can help with?'

questions.prompt: Best practice for verifying an inbound webhook signature (e.g. from Stripe)?

options.text: Compare HMAC over RAW body + timestamp; constant-time compare; reject if timestamp > 5 min old

questions.explanation: Parsing then reserializing can change bytes → HMAC mismatch. Timing-safe compare avoids side-channel attacks. Timestamp check prevents replay.

questions.prompt: Most production webhook systems choose at-least-once over exactly-once because:

options.text: Exactly-once needs distributed transactions + is too costly; at-least-once + idempotent consumers is simpler and reliable

questions.explanation: The receiver dedupes by idempotency_key. Trade the complexity of exactly-once semantics for the simplicity of at-least-once + client dedup.

questions.prompt: Client requires SAML SSO from their Okta and only allows their employees to reach your app. Design.

rubric.criterion: SP-initiated flow: user → app → redirect to Okta with SAMLRequest → assertion POST back → verify signature + issuer + audience + timing
Per-tenant IdP metadata (entity_id, x509 cert) stored + rotatable
Map SAML attributes (email, groups) → user + roles
JIT provisioning: first login creates user record
SCIM for lifecycle (deprovision on employee offboarding)
SLO (single logout) — or explicit note that we only do local logout
Tenant-restricted subdomain / IdP picker page

questions.modelAnswer: Multi-tenant. Login page routes by email domain to tenant's IdP config or shows picker at /sso/select. Use passport-saml or saml2-js. Per-tenant record: {sp_entity_id, idp_entity_id, idp_x509_cert, callback_url}. On response: validate signature, issuer, audience, timing (not-before, not-on-or-after), replay (store InResponseTo). Attributes → user: NameID → email, groups → roles. JIT: no user → create. SCIM v2 POST endpoint for Okta to push user lifecycle events. Cert rotation: support multiple valid certs during rollover.

questions.prompt: Implement SCIM v2 endpoint so Okta can auto-provision + deprovision users in your app.

rubric.criterion: SCIM v2 endpoints: /Users (POST create, GET list, GET/PATCH/PUT/DELETE by id) + /Groups
Authentication: bearer token issued per tenant, rotatable
PATCH support (partial updates via JSON Patch)
Filter query param support ('userName eq "x"')
Deprovision = soft delete + revoke sessions/tokens
Idempotency: repeated create with same externalId returns existing

questions.modelAnswer: Endpoints: POST /scim/v2/Users (create; if externalId exists, return existing with 200 not 201), GET /Users (paginated + filter), PATCH /Users/{id} (JSON Patch), DELETE /Users/{id} (soft delete + revoke all active sessions/refresh tokens + audit log). Same for /Groups. Per-tenant bearer token, rotatable via admin UI. Filter parser supports `userName eq`, `active eq`. Log every SCIM operation with source IP + user_agent + Okta org_id.

questions.prompt: Enterprise wants SSO with your app. They mention 'they've been on SAML for years.' When do you push for OIDC vs accepting SAML?

options.text: Accept SAML — if their IT is SAML-shop, forcing OIDC creates friction; both are secure. Push OIDC only if they don't already have SAML infra
OIDC only works for consumer apps

questions.explanation: Enterprise IT teams that already run Okta/PingFederate/AD FS have SAML integrations for hundreds of apps. Fighting that is a losing FDE battle. Support both.

questions.prompt: Which are REAL SAML security pitfalls to guard against? (select all)

options.text: Certificate rotation causing outages if not planned

questions.explanation: All real. XSW is the classic SAML CVE — attacker rewrites the assertion but keeps the signature. Use a well-audited library (passport-saml, saml2-js) with schema validation.

questions.prompt: Client's Okta admin says 'we're rotating our SAML signing cert next week.' How do you handle without downtime?

rubric.criterion: Get new cert BEFORE rotation date + store alongside old
Verifier accepts EITHER cert during rollover window
Retire old cert only after confirming all assertions signed with new
Audit log: which cert verified each assertion during window
Alert if old cert used within 7 days post-rotation

questions.modelAnswer: Get new cert now, add to trust store alongside old with rotation_date noted. Verifier tries new cert first, falls back to old. Log which cert verified each assertion. After 48h with zero old-cert verifications, remove old. Alert if any assertion during rollover window used unexpected cert (staging vs prod mixup).

questions.prompt: Client asks 'can we just push a CSV of users nightly instead of SCIM?' Response?

options.text: SCIM is real-time (deprovision on offboarding same day); CSV lags 24h. For security, insist on SCIM. Offer CSV import as ONE-TIME migration only.

questions.explanation: 24h lag on offboarding = an ex-employee retains access for a day. Compliance nightmare. SCIM v2 is the standard for a reason.

questions.prompt: Client CRM uses OAuth 1.0 and your platform uses OAuth 2.0. Design the bridge.

rubric.criterion: Adapter service between the two
Store client OAuth 1.0 tokens + secret encrypted (KMS) per user
Sign outbound requests with HMAC-SHA1 + nonce + timestamp per RFC 5849
User-facing app uses OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code + PKCE)
Token rotation, refresh handling, re-consent flow
Audit log + revoke path

questions.modelAnswer: Introduce Adapter Service. Users log in to our platform via OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code + PKCE). During onboarding, redirect through OAuth 1.0 flow to CRM: request-token → user authorizes → access-token. Encrypt (KMS) and store CRM tokens keyed by our user id. Adapter signs OAuth 1.0 requests per RFC 5849 whenever CRM API called. Health check + refresh flow. Revoke endpoint invalidates stored tokens.

questions.prompt: How do you store the customer's access tokens for the integrated service?

options.text: Encrypted with envelope encryption (data key from KMS), decrypted just-in-time

questions.explanation: AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Vault. Data key wraps token; only decryptable with KMS access. Rotate the master key without re-encrypting all data.

questions.prompt: Access token expired mid-call. How does the bridge recover?

rubric.criterion: Catch 401, use refresh token to get new access token
Store both new access + new refresh (many providers rotate refresh)
Retry original request with new token — single retry, no infinite loop
If refresh fails (invalid_grant), mark integration disconnected + notify user
Cache refresh in progress per user to avoid thundering herd

questions.modelAnswer: On 401: check if we have refresh_token, POST to /oauth/token with grant_type=refresh_token, store new access_token + new refresh_token (if provider rotates). Retry original request ONCE with new token. If refresh fails (invalid_grant / expired refresh), mark integration disconnected in DB + email user to re-authorize. Concurrency: distributed lock in Redis per user during refresh to prevent 10 requests all trying to refresh simultaneously.

questions.prompt: PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) is required when:

options.text: The client is a confidential server-side app
The client is public (SPA, mobile) and can't safely hold a secret — PKCE binds the auth code to a per-request verifier

questions.explanation: Now recommended for ALL OAuth 2.0 clients per OAuth 2.1 draft. Was originally for public clients only.

questions.prompt: Fortune 500 requires your AI platform to deploy INSIDE their AWS VPC with SSO via Okta + Snowflake as data source. Design.

rubric.criterion: All components in customer VPC — no cross-account API calls from data plane
IAM role assumption for cross-account access (no long-lived creds)
Egress: NAT gateway + explicit allowlist; log all outbound
Model serving: self-hosted vLLM/TGI, model weights in customer S3
Snowflake: PrivateLink connection
SSO: SAML from Okta, JIT provisioning
Terraform / CloudFormation for reproducible deploy

questions.modelAnswer: Everything runs in customer AWS account (Terraform-deployed). EKS cluster in private subnets. Model weights in customer S3 (SSE-KMS). vLLM pods pull weights on start. Egress: NAT gateway allowlist only Anthropic/OpenAI API endpoints (if hosted-LLM fallback used) or none at all (self-hosted only). Cross-account: our support team uses AssumeRole with MFA for time-limited access; audit logged. Snowflake via PrivateLink (no public internet). Okta SAML with JIT + SCIM for lifecycle. Ops dashboard hosted in customer VPC.

questions.prompt: Your engineers need occasional access to debug the customer-VPC deployment. How without permanent creds?

rubric.criterion: Customer creates IAM role trusting our AWS account
MFA required to assume role
Time-limited session tokens (1 hr max)
Just-in-time approval: request → customer approves → temp access
All actions logged to customer's CloudTrail + our audit

questions.modelAnswer: Customer creates an IAM role with trust policy allowing our AWS account's engineer role to assume it. External-ID prevents confused-deputy. Engineer requests access via ticket → customer approves via a workflow (e.g. Teleport) → time-limited session token issued (1 hr max) via STS AssumeRole with MFA. Every action logged to customer CloudTrail + shipped to our SIEM. No long-lived creds ever issued.

questions.prompt: Customer wants zero outbound network access from your app pods. What's the impact?

options.text: Doable — all models must be self-hosted; no telemetry to your own SaaS; observability sinks must run in-VPC (customer-hosted Grafana / Loki)

questions.explanation: Air-gapped VPC deploys are common in regulated industries. Every dependency must be internal. Model updates via customer-controlled S3 upload rather than pull-from-internet.

questions.prompt: Which deployment models can be offered to enterprise customers? (select all)
questions.explanation: Enterprise deals often require moving up this ladder based on data classification. Price increases 5-10x as you go up. Each mode changes your ops burden dramatically.

questions.prompt: Hospital wants a RAG chatbot over their internal clinical protocols + patient chart data (PHI). Design end-to-end with HIPAA in mind.

rubric.criterion: Business Associate Agreement (BAA) confirmed with every vendor touching PHI
All PHI stays in customer VPC — no third-party API for embed or generation
Encryption: at rest (KMS) + in transit (TLS 1.3)
Access control: retrieval filtered by requester's clinical role (attending / nurse / specialty)
Audit log: user, query, retrieved docs, response, timestamp — immutable
PHI redaction pre-embed OR encrypted-at-rest embeddings with access control
6-year retention per HIPAA — plan storage + purge

questions.modelAnswer: BAA in place with AWS, model vendor if any (else self-hosted), monitoring vendor. Entire pipeline in customer VPC: ingest, embed (self-hosted BGE), vector store (pgvector in Aurora), LLM (self-hosted Llama or clinical-fine-tuned in vLLM). Retrieval filter: `WHERE role IN (user.roles)` on doc-level metadata. Audit table append-only, 6-yr retention on S3 Glacier. PHI redaction with Presidio pre-embed; original still available to authorized roles via re-fetch by doc_id. Response includes citations to specific protocol sections.

questions.prompt: You're preparing for SOC2 Type II audit. Your app must provide auditor evidence for the 5 trust criteria. What do you set up?

rubric.criterion: Security: MFA everywhere, IAM least-privilege, encrypted at rest/transit, vuln scan
Availability: SLA measurement, incident response playbook + drills
Processing integrity: input validation, checksums, reconciliation jobs
Confidentiality: data classification, DLP, encryption keys managed
Privacy: consent, retention, deletion (right to be forgotten)
Automated evidence collection (Drata / Vanta / manual doc)
Continuous monitoring, not just point-in-time

questions.modelAnswer: Use Vanta/Drata to automate evidence collection. Security: enforce MFA org-wide, IAM audit monthly, TLS everywhere, monthly vuln scan + patch. Availability: SLO of 99.9%, incident runbook + quarterly game days. Processing integrity: input validation at API boundary, checksums on file transfers, nightly reconciliation with source systems. Confidentiality: data classification tags + encryption via KMS, DLP scan on outbound. Privacy: user-consent tracking, retention policies with automated purge, right-to-be-forgotten endpoint. Continuous evidence: agent collects daily, auditor sees 12 months at Type II.

questions.prompt: EU customer requires data residency (GDPR). Which are needed? (select all)

options.text: All storage + compute in EU AWS region
PII stays in EU even in logs / traces / backups
Model inference in EU if PII in prompts
DPA (Data Processing Agreement) signed with customer + any subprocessors

questions.explanation: Cross-region replication of PII (even encrypted) triggers GDPR restrictions post-Schrems-II. Everything (including observability + inference) must stay in EU when PII involved.

questions.prompt: Standard tool for PII detection + redaction in LLM pipelines:

options.text: Microsoft Presidio (open source, extensible with custom recognizers)

questions.explanation: Presidio handles emails, phones, SSNs, credit cards, names, dates, locations with NER. Regex alone misses many; manual doesn't scale.

questions.prompt: Client's 15-year-old on-premise ERP has no API. You need to integrate. Design.

rubric.criterion: Asks about DB access, existing batch exports, on-prem network access
Doesn't propose invasive rewrite — respects change control
Prefers CDC via replica > nightly file export > screen-scrape (last resort)
Extract into modern layer (S3 / warehouse), schema versioned
Two-way sync considerations + conflict handling
Audit + rollback plan

questions.modelAnswer: First ask: DB engine? Can we attach a read replica? Preferred: Debezium CDC from replica → Kafka → S3/warehouse. Fallback: nightly SQL exports as CSV to SFTP. For writes: if ERP has batch import files, submit through their window; else scope thin adapter service to whatever RPC/DB access is authorized. Changes require CAB (Change Advisory Board) approval respected. Audit every write with source + timestamp. Rollback: idempotent operations, revert file for each import.

questions.prompt: Client uses SAP ECC. You need real-time-ish sales order data. Options?

rubric.criterion: Names SAP integration options: IDoc, BAPI, OData (via Gateway), CDC on HANA
Recommends BASIS team engagement early
Uses SAP-native middleware if available (PI/PO, CPI)
Handles licensing / RFC user carefully (SAP audits these)
Never bypasses SAP transactions — always through supported interface
Failure of integration doesn't affect SAP performance

questions.modelAnswer: Depending on SAP setup: (1) IDoc — asynchronous, event-driven, well-audited. (2) OData via SAP Gateway — REST-ish, easier to consume. (3) CDC on underlying HANA DB if allowed (usually not by BASIS). (4) BAPI via SDK for synchronous calls. Recommend IDoc for our sales-order use case: SAP fires IDoc on order creation → our IDoc receiver → normalized event → our system. Engage BASIS team early — they own the RFC user, licensing implications, and change process. Rate-limit our consumer to avoid impacting SAP.

questions.prompt: CDC (Change Data Capture) via WAL/binlog vs nightly polling — CDC's main advantage:

options.text: Near-real-time changes with low DB overhead (reads the log, not the tables)

questions.explanation: Debezium reads WAL/binlog — near-zero load on source DB. Polling scans tables repeatedly, hurts source performance, has replication lag.

questions.prompt: Legacy system has ZERO API + no DB access permitted. Only option is screen-scraping (RPA-style). How do you make it reliable?

rubric.criterion: Flag as last resort — get sign-off in writing
Use resilient element selectors (data-testid > id > xpath position)
Snapshot testing: every run, compare screenshot to golden to detect UI change
Rate-limit + off-peak scheduling to avoid user impact
Retry with exp backoff on transient failures
Kill switch if error rate spikes (UI likely changed)

questions.modelAnswer: Screen-scrape is last resort — document as such and get sign-off. Use Playwright with the most stable selectors available (never brittle CSS position). Every run compares screenshots to golden set; UI diff > 5% alerts on-call and pauses. Rate-limit to 1 concurrent session, off-peak only. Retry with exp backoff on transient failures. Kill switch triggers if 3 consecutive runs fail — likely UI change. Weekly manual review of recorded flows.
